result:
Wrapping up. I've finished reading the code, both search artifacts, and the diagnostics run that completed during this review, so here is the verdict.

**Verdict: CONDITIONAL APPROVE** for the exposure/range scope, with the conditions listed at the end. The physics of the change is sound, the reachability evidence is now adequate for a bounded LVFW+SEP domain, and one prototype defect plus two labeling problems must be fixed before adoption.

## Overall assessment

The active multiplier scales Land Tref only. Tref enters the active stress and the active stiffness kernel as the same linear prefactor, and no kinetic state, calcium drive, passive law, or geometry changes. Scaling it to 0.25 is therefore mathematically clean. The research search confirms this numerically: all 48 exact evaluations were accepted, including four at or near 0.25, and every trial settled to period 1.

The three-coordinate search answers the reachability question decisively for this model family. Twenty-one points pass the disease screen, none meet the preferred EDVI 100 to 140 band, and the reason is visible in the data rather than inferred: on the fixed Klotz normal-center passive law with reference EDV 144 mL, mean LA reaches the 25 mmHg screen ceiling before EDVI reaches 100.

| Point (active / TBV / Rsys) | EDVI mL/m² | Mean LA mmHg | Screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.30 / 4935 / 1.04 | 95.8 | 22.9 | pass |
| 0.30 / 5122.5 / 1.00875 | 96.4 | 24.7 | pass |
| 0.25 / 5122.5 / 0.9775 | 97.4 | 26.4 | fail |

The proposal's refusal to add remodeling just to hit EDVI is correct. The EDVI miss should be registered as a limitation of fixed unloaded geometry, and reference-volume or wall-mass inputs deferred to a separate review.

The single-control diagnostics finished during this review and support the demo candidate at active 0.35 with baseline load. Cold 2 ms, cold 1 ms, and warm 2 ms agree closely, and restoring active to 1 at the same load reproduces the production baseline.

| Run | Cycles | EF % | EDVI | CI | Mean LA | Mean PAP | Mean Ao | Native LVEDP abs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cold 2 ms | 210 | 34.08 | 94.6 | 2.256 | 20.7 | 28.0 | 72.9 | 26.1 |
| cold 1 ms | 210 | 34.10 | 94.6 | 2.258 | 20.7 | 28.0 | 72.9 | 25.9 |
| warm 2 ms | 21 | 34.11 | 94.6 | 2.259 | 20.7 | 28.0 | 72.8 | 26.1 |
| active 1, cold | 54 | 55.75 | 75.6 | 2.952 | 8.4 | 17.9 | 93.6 | 10.9 |

This point passes the screen, meets the EF and CI targets, and misses EDVI by 5.4 mL/m². It is on the UI lattice. The best preregistered search point is not, and should not be adopted.

## Serious risks

**The candidate is congested, not compensated.** Native LVEDP of 26 mmHg absolute, mean LA of 21, and mean PAP of 28 describe acute non-remodeled contractile depression with pulmonary venous congestion and post-capillary pulmonary hypertension. The registry's own sources describe a different picture for outpatients: Moriwaki reports PAWP 12±8 and LVEDP 14±10, Shinke reports PAWP 11±7. The screen admits this point only because the design ceiling was set at 25. This does not change my approval, but it changes the label. The preset must be described as acute-like, non-remodeled, congested LV systolic depression, and the RVEF drop from 57% to 43% with RVFW unchanged must be visible as a septal and afterload consequence.

**The prototype's RVFW floor is 0.25, contrary to the proposal.** The derivative's validator exempts only LA and RA from the lowered minimum, so RVFW currently accepts 0.25 with no evidence. The global ventricular control derives its range from the same constant and would silently push RVFW to 0.25. Its error message also prints the wrong bound for atria. This must be fixed before any merge.

**Unexplored corners of the exposed domain.** No trial combined active 0.25 with Rsys 1.25 or TBV 5700, or with Rsys 0.75 and TBV 4200. A user can reach those corners in one slider drag. Earlier low-volume trials already produced mitral re-entry that broke the single-closure observer. Execution robustness at the corners is untested.

**Settling time and warm-start acceptance.** Cold settling at active 0.3 took 191 to 225 cycles against 54 for baseline. Large steps in the workbench will remain non-periodic for minutes of simulated time, and formal-periodic PV analysis will be stale. Separately, the warm diagnostics run was accepted after 21 cycles with a pulmonary-minus-aortic net-flow residual of 0.0038 L/min, two orders larger than the cold runs. Warm acceptance should require the same residual threshold.

**Warm route not yet tested from baseline.** The warm diagnostics case restored from the active 0.3 trial checkpoint, not from the Standard72 baseline checkpoint. The proposal's item 4 route, baseline then control operation then capture, has not been exercised.

**Capture parity cannot mean checkpoint hash equality across routes.** A capture is an atomic fixture plus checkpoint. Fixture equality after the control patch is deterministic and should be exact. A checkpoint reached by warm-start from baseline will never hash-match a cold-derived preset checkpoint. The condition needs to be split.

**Contractility wording.** The existing catalog consistently says 能動張力, never 収縮性. A grouped control named LV収縮性 invites the Ees reading the proposal wants to avoid. Use LV能動張力（自由壁＋中隔）and state that the septum is shared and that this is not a load-independent Ees.

## Smallest preferable scope and acceptance conditions

**Ownership decision.** Implement the grouped control as a kernel primitive control that patches LVFW and SEP together, mirroring how the existing common ventricular control patches three walls. The projection already returns mixed when walls differ, and the reducer already emits multi-path patches. The Surface knob schema exists but the workbench does not execute knobs, so using it here means writing a generic knob executor and knob capture semantics. That is the larger change and the wrong tradeoff for low complexity. Keep the Surface unchanged and reuse it, since control ranges live in the kernel catalog, not the Surface.

**Scope I approve, conditionally:**

1. New dev-stage model identity, new checkpoint ID, and new artifact build. Released 72's validator, checkpoint identity, and artifacts stay byte-identical. The derivative already does this correctly.
2. Active-tension floor 0.25 for LVFW and SEP only. RVFW, LA, and RA stay at 0.75 by per-wall minimum. The global ventricular control range becomes 0.75 to 1.33. The fixture's global contractility alias stays untouched at 1.
3. One grouped LV control, LVFW plus SEP, in the new model's default pane in place of LVFW alone. Individual wall controls remain in the full catalog. The new model gets its own control-count assertion rather than editing the Standard68 constant.
4. The demo candidate at active 0.35, TBV 4935, Rsys 1.04 as a dev-stage preset, described as acute-like non-remodeled congested LV systolic depression, with the EDVI miss recorded. No healthy gate claim, no publication.

**Conditions before adoption:**

- Fix the per-wall floor so RVFW rejects values below 0.75, and correct the validator message. Add a test that the global control cannot move RVFW below 0.75.
- Run an execution-robustness sweep over the eight domain corners plus the four 0.25 edges at extreme TBV and Rsys. Accepted execution with no non-finite state is required. Null contextual observations are acceptable if recorded with reason.
- Exercise the exact workbench route: Standard72 baseline checkpoint, apply the grouped control to 0.35, run to period-1 closure with the cold residual threshold, capture. Require the captured fixture to equal the preset fixture canonically. Require completed-beat metrics to agree with the cold preset within EF 0.1 percentage points, pressures 0.2 mmHg, and net-flow imbalance below 0.001 L/min. Then apply the control back to 1.0 and require the same agreement against the baseline.
- Give the preset checkpoint its own cold-replay parity evidence in the same form as the Standard72 binding evidence.
- Surface the periodic-classifier status in the workbench so users see when latest outputs and formal PV analysis are not yet periodic after a large step.
- Record Glantz tau as unavailable for this candidate rather than omitting it, since the fit fails at the shortened isovolumic window.

If the corner sweep fails at 0.25 but passes at 0.30, adopt a 0.30 floor instead. Every screen-passing trial lies at 0.30 or above, so 0.30 loses nothing for the demo and keeps the 0.25 exploration domain for a later review.
